papers.title: Electroweak Constraints on Nuclear Neutron Distributions and the Low-Energy Weak Mixing Angle
papers.abstract:
Coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) offers a low-energy probe of the weak mixing angle, $\sin^2	heta_W$, and possible new physics in the neutrino sector. Its reliable interpretation, however, requires independent constraints on the neutron distributions of the target nuclei. We exploit correlations across nuclei within an extended Skyrme energy-density-functional framework to propagate constraints from the CREX and PREX-II parity-violating electron-scattering (PVES) measurements to CE$
u$NS targets. This yields neutron form factors and radii, with relative radius uncertainties below $1\%$. Using these inferred neutron form factors, we jointly analyze the COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar data and obtain $\sin^2	heta_W=0.231^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$, consistent with the Standard Model prediction. These results provide the first electroweak-experimentally constrained benchmarks for nuclear-structure studies, neutrino-sector electroweak tests, and CE$
u$NS signal predictions in dark-matter detectors.
papers.reason: Connects parity-violating electron scattering constraints on neutron radii to COHERENT CEvNS data and the weak mixing angle, perfectly matching the reader's core interest in low-energy neutrino-nucleus interactions and electron scattering constraints.

summary.tldr: Combining PREX-II and CREX parity-violating electron scattering via an extended Skyrme EDF framework delivers tight neutron form-factor constraints, yielding $\sin^2\theta_W=0.231^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$ from a joint fit to COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar data.
summary.novel_idea: Previous CEvNS extractions of the weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_W$ suffered from strong degeneracies with target neutron distributions or relied on hadronic scattering inputs. This paper uses an extended Skyrme energy density functional (EDF) family with enhanced isovector spin-orbit interaction to reconcile the CREX and PREX-II PVES measurements, systematically propagating electroweak constraints to CEvNS target nuclei (${}^{133}\mathrm{Cs}$, ${}^{127}\mathrm{I}$, Ge isotopes, ${}^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$) to achieve relative point-neutron radius uncertainties below $1\%$.
summary.method: The authors constructed an extended Skyrme EDF family incorporating an enhanced isovector spin-orbit interaction with symmetry energy slope $L_c$ varied from 30 to 90 MeV (baseline IVSO250-Lc50). Standard Model weak charges with $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ electroweak radiative corrections were used to relate PVES charge-weak form factor differences $\Delta F_{\mathrm{CW}}$ across nuclei. Target point-neutron form factors $F_n(q)$ were fitted using Helm distributions, which were then deployed in a joint fit to reconstructed recoil spectra and timing distributions from COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar datasets.
key_results: Extracted point-neutron rms radii with $<1\%$ relative uncertainty for key CEvNS targets (e.g., $R_n = 4.887 \pm 0.038\mathrm{~fm}$ for ${}^{133}\mathrm{Cs}$, $3.468 \pm 0.031\mathrm{~fm}$ for ${}^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$, and $4.076 \pm 0.034\mathrm{~fm}$ for ${}^{74}\mathrm{Ge}$).

Determined the low-energy weak mixing angle to be $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.231^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$ at momentum transfer scale $\mu \sim 50\mathrm{~MeV}$ from a combined fit to COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar data.
Demonstrated that the precision gain is driven primarily by recent COHERENT Ge data, with the CsI+Ge joint fit yielding $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.227^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly targets core interests in CEvNS, nuclear weak form factors, electroweak radiative corrections, and extracting $\sin^2\theta_W$ from COHERENT data. Provides rigorous, PVES-calibrated Helm form factor inputs for neutrino event generators, low-energy interaction modeling, and dark matter detector predictions.
summary.caveats: Neglects nuclear spin-orbit current response terms in the CEvNS analysis (though shown to shift yields by only $\sim 0.2\text{--}0.4\%$). Relies on the assumption that an enhanced isovector spin-orbit interaction fully resolves the CREX-PREX puzzle across the nuclear chart.

papers.title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
papers.abstract: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints. keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity
papers.topic: Light mediators CEvNS and dark matter
papers.reason: Compares scalar and vector light mediator signatures across CEvNS, neutrino-electron scattering, and dark matter direct detection experiments, matching the reader's core interests in low-energy neutrino physics and BSM searches.

summary.tldr: Analyzes light scalar and vector mediators across CEvNS, electron scattering, and DM detection, showing that target degeneracies in Ge and Xe leave blind directions and demonstrating how neutrino background uncertainties shape the neutrino fog.
summary.novel_idea: Quantifies nuclear-target coupling degeneracies explicitly, demonstrating that combining ${}^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and ${}^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$ targets leaves nearly parallel blind directions due to a high condition number ($\sim 115$) of the nuclear-charge response matrix. It also introduces an analytic profile-likelihood framework to disentangle spectral overlap from external neutrino background constraints when evaluating dark-matter discovery limits in the neutrino fog.
summary.method: Formulates effective interaction models for light scalar (S1) and vector (V1, V2) mediators coupled to neutrinos, dark matter, and charged fermions. Computes differential cross sections for CEvNS (CsI, Ge, Xe, Ar), neutrino-electron scattering, and DM direct detection across momentum scales ($q \sim 3\text{--}99\mathrm{~MeV}$). Evaluates target complementarity using a two-target linear response analysis and models dark matter discovery sensitivity via an analytic profile-likelihood with Gaussian-information Fisher matrices.
key_results: Proved that the nuclear-charge response matrix for ${}^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and ${}^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$ has a condition number of $\approx 115$, demonstrating that multi-target CEvNS alone cannot resolve up- vs down-quark coupling degeneracies ($g_u$ vs $g_d$).

Derived an analytic expression $\Delta \sigma_{\alpha}^2 / \sigma_{\alpha}^2 = \rho^2 / [(1 - \rho^2)(1 + \lambda)]$ showing how dark-matter sensitivity degradation depends on spectral overlap $ho$ and external background constraints $\lambda$.

Mapped the distinct kinematic momentum transfer ranges probed by stopped-pion CsI ($35\text{--}99\mathrm{~MeV}$), solar Xe ($11\text{--}27\mathrm{~MeV}$), and reactor Ge ($3\text{--}12\mathrm{~MeV}$) detectors.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to research on BSM light mediator signatures at CEvNS experiments (COHERENT, CONUS+), liquid-xenon DM direct detection (LZ, XENONnT, PandaX-4T), and solar neutrino backgrounds.
summary.caveats: The profile-likelihood dark-matter sensitivity calculation is illustrative rather than a full experimental global fit, omitting multi-nuisance parameter profiling and detector-specific correlated systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Information content of the Gamow Teller Resonance: Bayesian inference with self-consistent Skyrme models
papers.abstract: Many important charge-exchange weak processes, such as beta decays, double beta decays, and neutrino-nucleus and neutrino-nucleon reactions, are closely related to the spin- and isospin-dependent nuclear force, yet few of them can be precisely measured, or even observed, in terrestrial experiments. The Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR) in finite nuclei is one of the few experimental probes of this spin-isospin force. In a companion letter, we obtained the probability distribution of the Landau-Migdal parameter $G'_0$, which characterizes the main part of the spin-isospin force, from GTR measurements using Bayesian inference. In this follow-up work, we quantitatively study the correlations emerging from this Bayesian analysis. From the posterior, we identify two standard Skyrme parameterizations (nuSky*) that reproduce, in a unified manner, ground-state observables of finite nuclei, the salient features of the GTR, and the bulk properties of neutron-star matter. Since collective excitations in finite nuclei and in neutron-star matter are related, we use the Skyrme interactions sampled from the posterior to constrain the axial-current, charged-current neutrino-nucleon reaction rates in hot and dense compact-star matter, as the first astrophysical application of this study. The GTR-informed calculations substantially reduce the spread of the neutrino opacity; nevertheless, significant uncertainties remain due to the poorly constrained symmetry energy at sub-saturation densities. Constraining this quantity on top of a well-constrained spin-isospin interaction would pave the way towards a systematic determination of neutrino interactions in dense matter.
papers.reason: Uses Bayesian inference with Skyrme models on Gamow-Teller resonance data to constrain neutrino-nucleon reaction rates and nuclear forces, perfectly matching core neutrino-nucleus and nuclear EFT interests.

summary.tldr: Uses Bayesian inference with Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR) data to constrain Skyrme EDFs (nuSky*), significantly reducing the Landau-Migdal parameter $G'_0$ uncertainty and axial-current neutrino-nucleon opacities in compact-star matter.
summary.novel_idea: Connects terrestrial Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR) measurements ($m_0\%$ and $E_{\mathrm{GT}}$ in ${}^{90}\mathrm{Zr}$, ${}^{132}\mathrm{Sn}$, ${}^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$) via a Bayesian posterior to astrophysical charged-current, axial-current neutrino-nucleon absorption rates in hot, dense compact-star matter. Identifies two new optimal Skyrme EDF parameterizations (`nuSkyI` and `nuSkyII`) that simultaneously describe ground-state nuclear properties, GTR spectra, and neutron-star matter bulk properties.
summary.method: Employed Charge-Exchange Random Phase Approximation (RPA) to compute GTR strength functions in finite nuclei and linear response theory in frequency space for uniform nucleonic matter. Performed Bayesian inference with intrinsic systematic error parameters over 25 experimental constraints (binding energies, charge radii, neutron skins, spin-orbit splittings, and GTR features). Propagated posterior Skyrme parameter sets (`GTAll`) to compute the RPA spin-isospin residual interaction parameter $G'_0$ and neutrino opacities in dense matter.
key_results: Constructed two new Skyrme parameterizations: `nuSkyI` ($L=53.4\mathrm{~MeV}$) and `nuSkyII` ($L=64.2\mathrm{~MeV}$), which satisfy ground-state, GTR, and high-density neutron star matter stability criteria.

Demonstrated that GTR constraints substantially narrow the posterior distribution of the Landau-Migdal parameter $G'_0$, heavily reducing the theoretical spread in charged-current axial neutrino opacity ($\mathrm{MB}_{ax}$).
Identified sub-saturation symmetry energy and the in-medium potential difference $\delta U = U_n - U_p$ as the remaining dominant source of neutrino opacity uncertainty in compact-star matter.
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant for nuclear density functional theory, spin-isospin electroweak response, Gamow-Teller transitions, and neutrino-nucleon/nucleus cross sections in supernova and neutron star merger environments.
summary.caveats: Does not account for cluster formation around the neutrinosphere, which can alter sub-saturation nucleon potentials and $\delta U$. Finite-nucleus GTR data cannot constrain the sub-saturation symmetry energy slope, leaving remaining vertical spread in opacity predictions.

papers.title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
papers.abstract:
Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{	au 4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $
u_	au$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $
u_	au$ scarcer, lowering the $
u_	au$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $
u_e$ or $
u_\mu$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{	au 4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.
papers.reason: Uses high-energy astrophysical neutrinos from IceCube to constrain tau-sterile neutrino mixing parameters over cosmological distances, squarely in core neutrino phenomenology.

summary.tldr: Demonstrates that mixing between tau and sterile neutrinos ($|U_{\tau 4}|^2$) reduces the high-energy astrophysical $\nu_\tau$ fraction at Earth, placing an IceCube limit of $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 < 0.88$ and projected multi-telescope bounds down to $0.12\text{--}0.14$.
summary.novel_idea:
Exploits the unique property of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos—where cosmic sources produce almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations generate $\sim 1/3$ $
u_	au$ at Earth—to probe $|U_{	au 4}|^2$ independently of sterile neutrino mass $\Delta m^2_{41}$. Proves that while $|U_{e4}|^2$ and $|U_{\mu 4}|^2$ can be absorbed or obscured by unknown source flavor ratios $f_{e,\mathrm{S}}$, tau-sterile mixing produces an unmistakable $
u_	au$ deficit that cannot be mimicked by source uncertainties.
summary.method: Used standard and 3+1 active-sterile neutrino oscillation probability frameworks over cosmological distances. Formulated a profile likelihood comparing predicted flavor compositions $(f_{e,\oplus}, f_{\mu,\oplus}, f_{\tau,\oplus})$ against 11.4-year IceCube MESE 2025 data and projected mock data for 2040 and 2050 multi-telescope arrays (IceCube, KM3NeT, Baikal-GVD, P-ONE, IceCube-Gen2, TRIDENT, HUNT). Profiled over active oscillation parameters (NuFIT 6.1) and source electron flavor fraction $f_{e,\mathrm{S}} \in [0,1]$.
key_results: Derived a 90% C.L. upper limit of $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 < 0.88$ from 11.4-year IceCube MESE data.
Projected multi-detector limits of $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 < 0.24\text{--}0.29$ by 2040 and $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 < 0.12\text{--}0.14$ by 2050 (for pion-decay sources).
Showed that 2050 multi-telescope combinations reach $3\sigma$ discovery potential if $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 \ge 0.23$ (pion decay) or $|U_{\tau 4}|^2 \ge 0.14$ (muon-damped sources).
Demonstrated robustness of limits against up to 10% $\nu_\tau$ emission at sources, non-zero $|U_{e4}|^2, |U_{\mu 4}|^2$, and inverted mass ordering.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant for BSM neutrino physics, sterile neutrino mixing limits ($|U_{\tau 4}|^2$), and astrophysical flavor-ratio phenomenology at current and future neutrino observatories (IceCube-Gen2).
summary.caveats: Sensitivity is fundamentally limited by the experimental $\nu_e\text{--}\nu_\tau$ degeneracy (showers produced by both flavors look similar in Cherenkov detectors). Relies on planned multi-kilometer-scale neutrino telescopes being completed as scheduled.

papers.title: Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER
papers.abstract: The ATOMKI anomalies motivate the possibility of a new particle, the X17, with a mass of 17 MeV and weak couplings to nuclei and electrons. Such a particle may be produced at the LHC, travel 480 m in the far-forward direction, and decay to $e^+e^-$ in FASER. In this paper, previous FASER searches for dark photons and axion-like particles (ALPs) are combined and interpreted as searches for a candidate X17 particle, the protophobic vector boson. The searches use data collected from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV in LHC Run 3 from 2022 for the dark photon search and from 2022-2023 for the ALP search. No excess events are found above the expected background, and the combined null results exclude a previously-unconstrained "low-coupling window" with electron coupling $6 \times 10^{-5} < \epsilon_e < 1.2 \times 10^{-4}$. A "high-coupling window" remains.
papers.reason: Combines FASER searches to constrain the protophobic X17 vector boson hypothesis, aligning well with BSM searches at forward neutrino/collider facilities. [favorite author: Felix Kling]

summary.tldr: Combining FASER's dark photon ($e^+e^-$ tracks) and ALP (preshower/calorimeter) searches excludes the low-coupling window ($6\times 10^{-5} < \epsilon_e < 1.2\times 10^{-4}$) for a 17 MeV protophobic vector boson (X17).
summary.novel_idea: Reinterprets and combines two orthogonal FASER Run 3 dataset searches—dark photons ($27\mathrm{~fb}^{-1}$) and ALPs ($57.7\mathrm{~fb}^{-1}$)—to cover the entire magnetized volume and preshower region of FASER for a protophobic vector boson candidate (X17). This provides the first LHC far-forward direct constraint that fully closes the low-coupling window of the X17 protophobic vector model.
summary.method: Modeled forward X17 production via proton bremsstrahlung (accounting for Dirac $F_1$ and Pauli $F_2$ form factors and damping factors) and $\eta \to X\gamma$ decays using FORESEE and CRMC/EPOS-LHC. Simulated $X \to e^+e^-$ decays inside FASER's active decay volume and downstream preshower/calorimeter regions. Constructed parameterized signal efficiencies for two-track and single-shower signatures, performing a profile likelihood $\mathrm{CL}_s$ combination at 90% C.L.
key_results: Observed zero events in the dark photon signal region and 1 event in the ALP signal region, consistent with expected SM backgrounds ($(2.3\pm 2.3)\times 10^{-3}$ and $0.44\pm 0.39$ events).
Excluded electron couplings $2\times 10^{-8} < \epsilon_e < 3\times 10^{-4}$ for $m_X = 17\mathrm{~MeV}$ and fixed neutron coupling $\epsilon_n = 10^{-2}$.
Excluded the previously unconstrained low-coupling ATOMKI window ($6\times 10^{-5} < \epsilon_e < 1.2\times 10^{-4}$), leaving only the high-coupling window ($\epsilon_e > 1.2\times 10^{-4}$) viable.
For the alternative protophobic model ($\epsilon_n = \epsilon_e = \epsilon$), excluded $2\times 10^{-5} < \epsilon < 1.5\times 10^{-4}$ at $m_X = 17\mathrm{~MeV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to BSM physics with light mediators, X17 anomaly explanations, LHC far-forward searches (FASER), and bounds on electron couplings of feebly interacting vector bosons.
summary.caveats: The high-coupling window ($\epsilon_e > 3\times 10^{-4}$) remains unconstrained by FASER because short lifetimes cause X17 to decay before reaching the 480 m forward detector. Assumes strict protophobic vector couplings ($\epsilon_p \approx 0, \epsilon_\nu \approx 0$).

papers.title: Topological Diagnostics of CP Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations with Non-Standard Interactions via Pancharatnam Open-Path Phases
papers.reason: Investigates topological signatures of non-standard interactions in long-baseline neutrino oscillations using geometric phases, fitting squarely into the reader's interest in oscillation systematics and BSM at neutrino experiments.

summary.tldr: Open-path Pancharatnam geometric phases in long-baseline neutrino oscillations resolve parameter degeneracies between Dirac CP violation and non-standard interactions.
summary.novel_idea: The paper extends the kinematic, open-path Pancharatnam-Mukunda-Simon geometric phase framework to non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) with off-diagonal vector couplings, demonstrating that energy-dependent spectral dispersions in the holonomies break continuous parameter degeneracies.
summary.method: A discrete-layer transfer matrix formalism and exact analytic eigensystem evaluation (Cardano-Zaglauer-Schwarzer) are applied across the $L = 1300	ext{ km}$ DUNE baseline configuration to compute neutrino and antineutrino transition amplitudes and branch-dependent holonomies.
key_results: Demonstrates that neutrino and antineutrino degeneracy bands intersect at non-parallel angles in the $(\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}, \phi_{e\tau})$ plane.
Confirms the robustness of the holonomy gradient signature under realistic LArTPC energy smearing (15-20%).
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to long-baseline oscillation systematics and DUNE sensitivity analyses concerning new physics degeneracies in the appearance channel.
summary.caveats: Restricted primarily to off-diagonal $\varepsilon_{e\tau}$ coupling and single-layer crust approximations, though the formalism supports multi-layer structures.

papers.title: Cosmic-Ray Signals from Dark Matter Annihilation into Scalars with Baryon Number
papers.abstract: Cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium-3 nuclei are promising probes of dark matter (DM). In light of potential detections of heavy antinuclei at AMS-02, we investigate a recently proposed scenario in which DM annihilates into color-singlet scalars carrying baryon and lepton number, which has been shown to enhance antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes relative to antiprotons. Accounting for Galactic propagation and detector sensitivities, we calculate the number of events predicted by our model for parameters that are compatible with the seven-year AMS-02 antiproton data. Broad regions of the DM-mediator mass plane result in observable antideuteron fluxes at AMS-02 and GAPS. While detecting antihelium-3 remains more challenging, potentially detectable fluxes can arise for light mediators and moderately light DM, and in general are enhanced relative to the standard WIMP predictions. Furthermore, we find antihelium-to-antideuteron event ratios of O(0.1), closer to those suggested by the reported AMS-02 candidate events than conventional WIMP predictions.
papers.reason: Investigates cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium from dark matter annihilation into baryonic scalars, highly relevant to dark sector searches and cosmic-ray signatures.

summary.tldr: Dark matter annihilation into baryon-number-carrying scalars enhances heavy antinuclei fluxes, yielding observable signals at AMS-02 and GAPS.
summary.novel_idea: Investigates a $B=L=3$ dark sector model where DM annihilates into multi-quark scalar cascades, generating an enhanced antimatter yield that bypasses traditional WIMP coalescence suppression.
summary.method: Pythia 8 Monte Carlo event generation coupled with a calibrated coalescence model and a semi-analytical two-zone Galactic propagation framework constrained by AMS-02 antiproton data.
key_results: Found broad regions of the $(m_{\phi}, m_{\text{DM}})$ parameter space yielding observable antideuteron fluxes at AMS-02 and GAPS for thermal-relic cross sections.
Predicted antihelium-to-antideuteron event ratios of $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$, which are closer to reported AMS-02 candidate events than standard WIMP predictions.
summary.why_it_matters: Addresses indirect detection constraints and dark sector signatures using cosmic-ray antinuclei data directly relevant to ongoing searches.
summary.caveats: Best-fit cross sections for the Galactic Center gamma-ray excess exceed AMS-02 antiproton limits under standard NFW assumptions.

papers.title: Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons
papers.abstract: The years preceding a supernova (SN) can constrain new electrophilic bosons with MeV masses more than the explosion itself. Although cooler than SNe, the massive progenitors maintain consistently high temperatures much longer, injecting more particles whose decays to positrons contribute to the diffuse Galactic 511-keV emission. For dark photons, the increase is exacerbated by the lower plasma frequency compared to SNe, where MeV excitations are screened. We find preSNe bounds on dark photon couplings up to two orders of magnitude stronger than SNe for masses between 1 and 3~MeV, with similar improvements for other electrophilic species such as axion-like particles.
papers.reason: Constrains MeV-scale electrophilic dark bosons and ALPs using pre-supernova stellar temperatures and cooling, directly hitting the reader's interest in supernova neutrinos and stellar probes of BSM physics.

summary.tldr: Pre-supernova stellar evolution provides stronger constraints on electrophilic MeV bosons than the core-collapse explosion itself.
summary.novel_idea: Utilizes the prolonged high-temperature carbon, oxygen, and silicon burning phases of massive stellar progenitors as continuous sources of feebly interacting particles that decay into positrons contributing to the Galactic 511-keV line.
summary.method: Evolutionary tracks of 9-$60\,M_{\odot}$ stars simulated using MESA to extract temperature-density profiles, combined with analytic thermal emission rates for dark photons and axion-like particles and positron propagation smearing.
key_results: Derived exclusion limits on dark photon mixing parameters down to $\varepsilon \simeq 10^{-14}$ for masses between 1 and 3 MeV.
Improved upon existing supernova bounds (such as from SN 1987A and SN 2023ixf) by up to two orders of magnitude.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a novel astrophysical constraint mechanism using pre-supernova stages that transcends traditional supernova cooling bounds.
summary.caveats: Assumes negligible backreaction of dark photon cooling on stellar structure and depends on uncertainties in Galactic positron propagation lengths.

papers.title: Searching for Long-Lived Dark Scalars with MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 at the HL-LHC
papers.abstract: Feebly interacting particles (FIPs) arise generically in dark-sector extensions of the Standard Model (SM). Among the simplest and most theoretically motivated such candidates is a dark scalar that mixes with the SM Higgs boson, acting as a mediator between the dark sector and the SM. For sufficiently small mixing, such a dark scalar manifests at collider experiments as a long-lived particle with a macroscopic decay length---a signature to which conventional general-purpose detectors have limited sensitivity. The MoEDAL-MAPP experiment is a dedicated search facility at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) targeting long-lived FIPs as avatars of physics beyond the SM. We present $95\%$ confidence-level background-free sensitivity projections for the MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 detectors at the High-Luminosity LHC to Higgs-portal dark scalars produced via rare $B$-meson decays and exotic Higgs boson decays. Our results establish the proposed MAPP-2 detector as a complementary probe of feebly-coupled dark scalars, with sensitivity to lifetimes beyond the reach of existing collider searches.
papers.reason: Projects sensitivity for feebly interacting dark scalars at the MoEDAL-MAPP detector at the HL-LHC, matching interests in collider FIP searches and dark sector portals.

summary.tldr: The MAPP-2 detector at the HL-LHC offers high sensitivity to long-lived Higgs-portal dark scalars via displaced vertex searches.
summary.novel_idea: Provides the first comprehensive sensitivity projections for MAPP-2 incorporating both rare $B$-meson decays and exotic Higgs boson decays into feebly coupled dark scalars.
summary.method: Monte Carlo simulations using Pythia 8 to model dark scalar production via $B \to K\phi$ and $h \to \phi\phi$, combined with decay-length calculations and geometric fiducial acceptance tracking for MAPP-1 and MAPP-2.
key_results: MAPP-1 probes mixing angles down to $\sin\theta \sim 10^{-7}$, while MAPP-2 extends sensitivity down to $\sin\theta \sim 10^{-8}$ for masses $2m_\mu \lesssim m_\phi \lesssim m_h/2$.
Establishes background-free $95\%$ CL limits assuming a benchmark Higgs decay branching ratio $\mathcal{B}(h \to \phi\phi) = 0.01$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts BSM physics searches at neutrino and long-lived particle facilities like the LHC, showcasing dedicated outrigger/gallery detector capabilities.
summary.caveats: Projections assume a background-free environment and a 100% signal reconstruction efficiency with an idealized dimuon branching fraction.

papers.title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
papers.abstract: The simultaneous determination of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and fundamental physical parameters, e.g. the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$, the mass of the top quark $m_t$, or Wilson coefficients of an Effective Field Theory operators, is essential for the high-precision physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider. Yet, simultaneous global fits face significant methodological and computational challenges, rooted in the fundamental tension between estimating a finite-dimensional parameter and an infinite-dimensional function. In this paper, we address this problem by introducing a semiparametric estimation framework. The key advantage of our approach is that it avoids the need to refit the PDFs in the presence of either modified SM parameters or BSM contributions. Starting from standard, decoupled estimates of the PDFs and physics parameters, the method computes a bias correction a posteriori via the efficient influence function, yielding a debiased one-step estimator of the finite-dimensional parameter along with uncertainties with valid frequentist coverage. This correction rigorously accounts for the interplay between PDF and physics parameters without requiring a computationally expensive joint fit. As a proof of concept, we apply the method to two toy scenarios preparatory to a realistic global fit: the extraction of a dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficient from Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) pseudo-data based on BCDMS measurements, isolating the non-singlet PDF combination $T_3$, and to the determination of the proton total valence $V$ from combined HERA measurements. Our results demonstrate that the one-step estimator successfully removes the bias inherent in a preliminary, decoupled estimate and achieves confidence intervals with correct nominal coverage, offering a statistically rigorous and computationally efficient alternative to full simultaneous PDF fits.
papers.reason: Introduces a semiparametric framework to simultaneously determine PDFs and SMEFT Wilson coefficients without full refitting, highly relevant to precision global fits and EFT analyses.

summary.tldr: A semiparametric estimation framework avoids full simultaneous PDF fits when extracting physics parameters like EFT Wilson coefficients.
summary.novel_idea: Introduces an efficient influence function to compute an a posteriori bias correction, yielding a debiased one-step estimator for finite-dimensional parameters in the presence of infinite-dimensional PDF nuisance parameters.
summary.method: Constructs B-spline basis expansions for PDFs combined with linear deep inelastic scattering (DIS) forward maps and efficient score projections evaluated on BCDMS and HERA pseudo-data.
key_results: Demonstrated successful removal of estimation bias in extracting a dimension-6 SMEFT Wilson coefficient and the proton valence distribution $V$.
Achieved frequentist confidence intervals with correct nominal coverage without requiring computationally heavy joint PDF refits.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a statistically rigorous and computationally efficient tool for precision electroweak and BSM parameter extraction where PDF uncertainties dominate.
summary.caveats: Demonstrated primarily on linear DIS toy models, leaving bilinear hadronic (proton-proton) processes for future work.

papers.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
papers.abstract: We measure the $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $\pi^+\pi^-/\mu^+\mu^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_{\mu}^{\pi\pi}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.
papers.topic: BaBar e+e- to pi+pi- cross section
papers.reason: Provides a precise measurement of the $e^+e^-	o	ext{pi}^+	ext{pi}^-$ cross section via ISR to constrain hadronic vacuum polarization for muon $g-2$, highly relevant to precision low-energy standard model tests.

papers.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
papers.abstract: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to \pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$\Upsilon(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $\pi^+\pi^-$ to $\mu^+\mu^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.
papers.reason: Identical or companion paper to 2611.04596 reporting precise BaBar results for hadronic vacuum polarization and muon $g-2$ inputs.

papers.title: Twist-three quark TMDs from back-to-back dijet production in next-to-eikonal DIS
papers.abstract: We study back-to-back dijet production in deep inelastic scattering (DIS) at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on the quark-background contributions. We compute the quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections through next-to-leading power in the correlation limit for longitudinally and transversely polarized photons. In the quark-gluon channel, we derive both the kinematic corrections to the hard parts accompanying the twist-two quark distribution and the genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators. In the quark-antiquark channel, the interference of the eikonal amplitude with the double $t$-channel quark-exchange amplitudes probes three-body correlators with a different transverse arrangement of the fields. We express the results in terms of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlators and provide the corresponding hard coefficients. Our analysis extends the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark TMDs beyond leading power in the correlation limit.
papers.reason: Computes twist-three quark TMD correlators and dijet production in DIS within the Color Glass Condensate framework, highly relevant to nucleon structure and advanced DIS scattering theory.

papers.title: Projected sensitivity of the \anubis detector to photophobic and fermion-coupled axion-like particles
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are a common benchmark for experiments at the lifetime frontier, as their suppressed couplings to Standard Model particles can render them long-lived on detector scales. This article presents the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to two scenarios: a photophobic ALP model and a modified version of the flavour-diagonal, fermion-coupled ALP benchmark of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative that introduces an additional $h\to Za$ decay. For the photophobic case, the ANUBIS detector will reach a peak sensitivity of $\sigma_{Wa}\cdot Br(a\rightarrow gg)=6.2\times10^{-4}$~pb at $c\tau=1.95$ m for an ALP mass of $10$ GeV. This will improve on the current exclusion limits from the ATLAS experiment by two orders of magnitude and extend the $c\tau$ coverage by three orders of magnitude. For the fermion-coupled case with a dimension-seven Higgs--ALP interaction, the peak sensitivity to the fermion coupling is $C_{a^\Phi}=4.4\times10^{-8}$, reached for ALP masses between $16$ and $23$ GeV. Overall, the ANUBIS detector is shown to provide unique coverage of the parameter space of both models, in regions that can be probed neither by the main LHC experiments nor by forward detectors at the HL-LHC.
authors: Paul Swallow for the ANUBIS Collaboration
papers.reason: Evaluates projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the HL-LHC to long-lived axion-like particles, directly aligning with BSM physics at neutrino/particle experiments.

papers.title: GUT Color-Triplet Around the Corner: The Story of an Overlooked Lightness
papers.abstract: In traditional approach to the doublet-triplet splitting problem in grand unified theories (GUTs) it is assumed that color-triplet partner of the Higgs doublet must be superheavy in order not to mediate proton decay. However, it has been proposed [1] that the splitting, instead of the mass sector, can occur among the Yukawa couplings. In this scenario the color-triplet emerges as a long-lived $T$-particle with the mass around the TeV scale. This framework provides a direct low-energy window into GUT physics. In the present paper, we study an explicit supersymmetric $SO(10)$ GUT which realizes this mechanism, including effects of gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking. We show how the shift of the heavy fields, triggered by supersymmetry-breaking, generates a tiny coupling between the $T$-particle and the Standard Model fields and explore the resulting phenomenology. Depending on the order of gravitino mass in which the coupling emerges, the lifetime of the $T$-particle is either around a second or exceeds the age of the Universe. In our analysis, we validate some earlier constraints on (super)gravity vacua imposed by the $S$-matrix: based on the Goldstino Argument, we show that none of the GUT vacua have positive energy densities, whereas the Minkowski vacua are safe against tunneling. We also highlight the role of the species scale cutoff in sensitivity of the low energy observables towards the GUT physics.
papers.reason: Explores a TeV-scale color-triplet scalar from GUTs with low-energy phenomenological consequences, aligning well with precision BSM and low-energy portals.

papers.title: Shortcomings of the squark simplified model
papers.abstract: We argue that the squark simplified model commonly used in collider analyses fails to represent realistic low-energy supersymmetric models and significantly underestimates squark production rates at hadron colliders. This has important implications for extracting squark mass limits at the LHC and assessing the potential reach of HL-LHC or the FCC-hh. In particular, we find that the current LHC squark mass limit is realistically in the range of 2.6-3.0 TeV, rather than the 1.7-1.8 TeV range that is typically quoted based on the simplified model.
papers.reason: Critiques collider simplified models for squarks and argues for substantially higher mass limits, relevant to collider BSM constraints.

papers.title: Parametrization of unitary matrices, parametrizing the symmetric $S$ matrix and the $NN$ $S$ matrix above the inelastic threshold
papers.abstract: None of the $S$-matrix representations used in analyses of nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) scattering above the inelastic threshold is implicitly unitary, general, and connected to low-energy (Stapp) parameters, and hence correspondingly related to the physical properties of the scattering. Such a representation is also needed to solve the corresponding inverse scattering problem. I present an $S$-matrix representation which satisfies these requirements. As a by-product, I derive a parametrization of an $n$-dimensional unitary matrix.
papers.reason: Derives an implicitly unitary parametrization of the nucleon-nucleon S-matrix above inelastic thresholds, relevant to nucleon-nucleon interactions and scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Axion Electrodynamics in Presence of a Stellar Non-homogeneous Background Magnetic Field
papers.abstract: We re-assess effects of Axion Electrodynamics in the presence of non-homogeneous background magnetic fields. The Primakoff effect, which is an ALP-photon mixing induced by a background magnetic field, is generalized to the case of non-homogeneous backgrounds. The production of ALPs from a magnetized plasma thermal medium is also computed. The Eddington's solar standard model is adopted as the phenomenological scenario for our settings, and new bounds on the Axion Electrodynamics parameter space are imposed by considering helioseismological and neutrino observational measurements.
papers.reason: Re-assesses axion-photon mixing and ALP production in stellar magnetic backgrounds using solar models and neutrino/helioseismological bounds.

papers.title: Modeling a Framework for Comprehensive Analysis of $\boldsymbol{p^\uparrow\!{A}}$ Transverse Analyzing Power Measurements at the RHIC HJET
papers.abstract: We present a model for calculating the forward elastic analyzing power $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in proton-nucleus scattering, based on the Glauber approximation and incorporating soft-photon exchange corrections. The model is tested against 100 GeV HJET measurements for several nuclei, including Au, Ru, Zr, Al, O, C, and the deuteron. The calculations use Woods-Saxon parameters to describe the nuclear density distributions, as well as the proton-proton and proton-neutron hadronic spin-flip amplitudes, with the latter constrained by a Regge fit to HJET $pp$ data. Using the nominal input parameters, the calculations provide a reasonable description of the measured analyzing powers, although further refinement is needed to achieve a satisfactory fit. Allowing the input parameters to vary in the fits substantially improves the agreement with the data, yielding effective parametrizations of $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in terms of three or four parameters, depending on the nucleus. Notably, the nominal values of the imaginary part of the effective proton-nucleus spin-flip parameter $r_5^{pA}$ agree well with the fitted values for all nuclei considered. Subject to the limitations of the present model, this observation concerning $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ is consistent with the proton-proton spin-flip amplitudes measured at HJET and supports the interpretation of a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling. The results presented in this paper also motivate further investigation of the energy dependence of the proton-nucleon spin-flip amplitude using HJET measurements over a broad range of beam energies, with potential applications to proton-carbon and \(^3\)He polarimetry at the Electron-Ion Collider.
papers.reason: Models forward elastic analyzing power in proton-nucleus scattering using Glauber approximation and hadronic spin-flip amplitudes, relevant to nuclear scattering mechanisms.

papers.title: Revisiting the gamma-ray signal from light ALPs emitted during the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs
papers.abstract: The memory-burden effect was recently proposed to take into account the information back-reaction in the evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs). In this work, we systematically explore the axion-like particle (ALP) production via the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs and the subsequent ALP-photon conversion in cosmic magnetic fields. The PBH evaporation progress is divided in the semiclassical phase of Hawking radiation and the quantum memory-burden phase. The time evolution of PBH mass and the gamma-ray flux after the conversion of PBH-emitted ALP are then evaluated by considering the memory-burden induced PBH entropy suppression. Furthermore, we investigate the detection prospects of this evaporation-conversion signal in next-generation satellite telescopes, including AMEGO, e-ASTROGAM and MAST. The detectable PBH mass range is extended down to masses much smaller than $10^{15}$ g. Applying the Fisher forecasting method, we derive the projected sensitivity for PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$ and ALP-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$.
papers.reason: Explores ALP production from primordial black hole evaporation with memory-burden effects and subsequent photon conversion, connecting to cosmological dark matter probes.

papers.title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis
papers.abstract: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field dissipation and friction on cosmic walls through interactions with the radiation background. We study the conditions under which these effects are negligible and map the parameter regions yielding observable GW signals onto the usual ALP mass-coupling parameter space. We find that, in these regions, ALPs dominate the energy density of the Universe before they decay, leading to a period of intermediate matter domination, which would leave a clear imprint on the GW spectrum.
papers.reason: Calculates gravitational wave signatures from cosmic string-wall network annihilations in unstable ALP models, relevant to cosmological dark matter phenomenology.

papers.title: Modeling fragmentation of $^{20}$Ne nuclei at the LHC
papers.abstract: Fragmentation of relativistic neon nuclei was studied with the Abrasion-Ablation Monte Carlo for Colliders model (AAMCC-MST), which incorporates pre-equilibrium clustering of spectator matter via a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) algorithm, subsequent decays of the excited clusters, and Coulomb repulsion between final fragments. After validating the model against data on $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne fragmentation on various targets, the production of spectator nuclear fragments, neutrons, and protons in $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne collisions at the LHC was modeled at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$ TeV. The production cross sections, transverse and longitudinal momentum distributions for $^2$H, $^4$He, $^6$Li, $^{10}$B, $^{12}$C, $^{14}$N, and $^{16}$O fragments were calculated as these fragments may contaminate $^{20}$Ne beams circulating in the LHC. A simple parametrization describing relative width of the longitudinal momentum distributions calculated for these fragment species was constructed. To study the sensitivity of results to $\alpha$-clustering and nuclear density distributions in neon nuclei, two density profiles for $^{20}$Ne and $^{22}$Ne were used: a deformed Woods-Saxon, and a five-$\alpha$ bi-pyramidal configuration. In addition, a spherical profile was considered for $^{20}$Ne. Comparing results obtained with these profiles and with or without MST clustering shows that the calculated yields of spectator nucleons and fragments, their momentum distributions are sensitive to the details of nuclear structure of $^{20,22}$Ne and fragmentation modeling. The results provide the input for simulations of the transport of secondary forward nuclei in the LHC to estimate their interaction rates with circulating $^{20}$Ne beam nuclei, and also for calculations of responses of neutron and proton Zero Degree Calorimeters to $^{20}$Ne-$^{20}$Ne events.
authors: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology
Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology
Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology
papers.topic: Modeling fragmentation of Ne-20 at LHC
papers.reason: Models relativistic neon fragmentation with clustering and abrasion-ablation algorithms for LHC collisions, relevant to nuclear beam backgrounds and nuclear structure/fragmentation models.

papers.title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+\Lambda\Lambda$ reaction
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ \Lambda \Lambda\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(\pi\), \(\eta\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho\), \(\omega\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(\eta\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.
papers.topic: Nucleon resonances in pp to KKLambdaLambda
papers.reason: Investigates nucleon resonances and double-resonance mechanisms in associated strangeness production using an effective Lagrangian approach, relevant to baryon spectroscopy.

papers.title: Electroweak corrections to the SM-like Higgs boson decays and the Higgs trilinear coupling in the real Higgs triplet model
papers.abstract: We study new physics effects on the decays of the standard model-like Higgs boson ($h$) and the Higgs trilinear coupling including the full one-loop corrections in the real Higgs triplet model (RHTM). We adopt the on-shell renormalization scheme, in which the scalar mixing angles are renormalized in a gauge-independent way using the pinch technique. We found that sizable one-loop effects can arise in the decay rates through the Higgs wave-function (external-leg) corrections, while the tree-level effects are rather small due to the constraint on the vacuum expectation value of the triplet field from the electroweak precision measurements. In addition, the $h\to\gamma\gamma$ decay rate and the $hhh$ coupling are sensitive to loop contributions. The RHTM may be distinguishable from other extended Higgs models by studying the correlations among the $h\to\tau\tau$, $h\to ZZ^{*}$, and $h\to\gamma\gamma$ decay modes, and such characteristic predictions can be tested at the High-Luminosity LHC or future Higgs factories.
papers.topic: Electroweak corrections in Higgs triplet model
papers.reason: Computes full one-loop electroweak corrections to Higgs decays and trilinear couplings in the real Higgs triplet model using a gauge-independent scheme, aligning with precision electroweak physics and extended Higgs sectors.

papers.title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.abstract: A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected during 2016$-$2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ and [4.8 (3.0)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] $\times$10$^{-6}$ and [2.4 (1.3)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dimuon channel.
papers.reason: Searches for heavy neutral leptons (majorana HNLs) in CMS top decays, directly fitting the BSM at neutrino and collider experiments interest.

papers.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
papers.abstract: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.
papers.reason: Constructs nonlinear electroweak vector hair around Schwarzschild black holes in the Weinberg-Salam theory, of moderate interest due to non-Abelian gauge-Higgs field configurations.

papers.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
papers.abstract: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.
papers.reason: Reports an experimental bound on low-energy light-by-light scattering using X-ray lasers and high-intensity optical fields, relevant to vacuum birefringence and QED precision tests.

papers.title: Non-uniqueness of the amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem and a refinement of Hoehler's resonance clustering
papers.abstract: Reaction-amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem is limited by the bilinear form of all reaction observables. At fixed kinematics, N complex amplitudes contain 2N real quantities, whereas complete measurements determine at most 2N-1 parameters. Uniqueness therefore depends on whether additional physical constraints, such as unitarity, supply the missing information. We examine the consequences for resonance identification, focusing on angular-momentum assignments. Building on published results showing how truncation redistributes pole-bearing contributions among effective partial waves, we examine exact and practical ambiguities associated with imposing coupled-channel unitarity. A 4 x 4 counterexample shows that different on-shell unitary amplitudes can produce identical measurable bilinears. Practical unitary descriptions can also yield different pole content while remaining compatible with experimental uncertainties. We update Hoehler's clustering using the thirteen four-star N* resonances in PDG 2026 and Bonn-Gatchina results published in 2025. Nearby poles with different partial-wave assignments occur both in the PDG compilation and within Bonn-Gatchina, so their proximity is not solely a consequence of PDG averaging. Some groupings persist, while others change appreciably. We discuss a conditional interpretation in which truncation redistributes a common pole-bearing contribution among effective partial waves, with additional reconstruction uncertainties potentially accounting for departures from coincident pole positions. These considerations allow, but do not establish, a common origin for cluster members. The necessity of separate states and the stability of their angular-momentum assignments remain questions for further investigation.
papers.reason: Examines ambiguities and unitarity constraints in reaction-amplitude reconstruction and resonance clustering for nucleon states, relevant to scattering theory.

papers.title: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation
papers.abstract: An important physical quantity that is part of the Saha ionisation equation is the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. An immense uncertainty is caused by the divergency of the neutral atom partition function arising due to the fast growing degeneracy factor of its excited n-state. We suggested a regularisation and renormalisation procedure for the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. The renormalised partition function is well defined and allows to calculate the population of the energy levels and the ionisation state of the hydrogen plasma as a function of its temperature and pressure. In the low-temperature limit the behaviour of these functions smoothly transforms to the Saha equation, which is used in the description of the low-temperature plasma. At higher temperatures the renormalised ionisation equation describes the deviation from the Saha equation. The application of the renormalised ionisation equation to the solar core and atmosphere is considered.
papers.reason: Provides a regularization and renormalization procedure for the neutral hydrogen atom partition function and Saha equation, intersecting atomic/plasma precision physics.

papers.title: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment
papers.abstract: We consider a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed in a quantum field and investigate how motion affects the quantum coherence of its internal degrees of freedom, manifesting as quantum dispersion in the absence of a quantum field, and decoherence in its presence. Our investigation aims to serve two purposes: One is to obtain the correct results for these effects, which are essential for the design of quantum information processing schemes where the quantum coherence of an atom's internal degrees of freedom is of major concern. The other is to expose the fallacies in commonplace approaches, which start with a non-relativistic calculation and then add on relativistic ``corrections". We first show a fully relativistic calculation of the internal dynamics based on covariance principles, and then one which ignores these principles, often justified by the atom's slow motion. By a direct comparison of results from these two approaches, we identify {significant discrepancies} in a non-relativistic treatment, even at low atomic speeds. The proper procedure, and a much safer one in terms of accuracy, is recommended here: first derive the dynamics and the necessary regularizations within a fully covariant relativistic framework. Only after the exact, internally consistent equations of motion are established should low-velocity limits be extracted from them. Only in this way can all the relativistic effects which matter: time dilation, aberration, non-inertial mass shifts, be systematically preserved, and accurate results obtained.
papers.reason: Investigates fully relativistic treatments of motional decoherence of internal atomic states interacting with quantum fields, highly relevant to precision atomic probes and quantum sensors.

papers.title: Can multi-level Monte-Carlo address the sign problem in a finite-density Bose gas?
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation of field theories with complex actions is frustrated by the sign problem, which causes an exponential growth in statistical sampling noise. A key example of such a theory is QCD at finite baryon chemical potential, which has important applications to the structure of atomic nuclei and neutron stars. Until now, the sign problem has precluded the possibility of first-principles numerical calculations that could provide key insight into these important physical systems. In this work, we propose an approach to avoiding this limitation by applying a reweighting procedure coupled with a multi-level Monte-Carlo sampling algorithm that offers an exponential enhancement of statistics to counteract the sign problem. We test the approach on a simpler model that displays the same sign problem at finite chemical potential. Our results demonstrate the promise of the proposed approach, significantly increasing the range over which precise calculations are possible, and providing improvements all the way up to the phase transition.
papers.reason: Proposes a multi-level Monte-Carlo sampling algorithm combined with reweighting to address the sign problem in finite-density Bose gases, highly relevant to lattice methods for dense nuclear matter.

papers.title: Native transverse-momentum evolution and matching for TMD factorization and extraction
papers.abstract: We present a native transverse-momentum realization of the Collins/CSS2 leading-power transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization framework. The construction connects fixed-order distributional matching, origin contacts, unexpanded two-scale evolution, and a differentiable interface for hadronic structure. An endpoint-independent canonical scale with a specified infrared completion generates a Collins--Soper kernel on a common invariant domain. Complete canonical legs are bounded and admit constructive momentum-space evaluation through resolvent convolutions or elliptic solves. We give contact and finite-bin error bounds, parent-to-momentum-boundary translations, ordered flavor recurrences, and an all-order argument for the four exponent towers of $N^3\mathrm{LL}$ evolution. Localized joint-$(x,k_T)$ inputs, nonperturbative rapidity broadening, regulated moments and the full-spectrum subtraction are formulated as distinct parts of the prescription. The physical realization uses sourced four-loop beta/cusp and three-loop noncusp/Collins--Soper ingredients with strict-NLO hard/OPE boundaries. Non-Gaussian continuum tests and three-scale physical-PDF comparisons validate ordinary legs, contacts, individual insertions and analytic input derivatives. Including a declared bound on the continuation above a finite PDF table, physical bin discrepancies remain below $4.27\times10^{-5}$ of the peak reference bin. A qualified proton--proton Drell--Yan and neural-closure demonstration connects the method to inverse use. Higher-order boundary assembly and matched observables are specified without claiming an implemented $N^3\mathrm{LL}'$ spectrum or a completed global extraction.
papers.reason: This is a detailed formal paper on transverse-momentum-dependent factorization and matching, which is adjacent to the reader's interest in parton showers and QCD for lepton-nucleus scattering.

papers.title: Holographic spin alignment of vector mesons in a spinning black-hole background
papers.abstract: Holographic predictions for vector-meson spin alignment are difficult to compare between charmonium and light vector mesons, as the two sectors are typically treated in different rotating backgrounds and spectral prescriptions. Consequently, it remains unclear whether a single rotating medium can generate the opposite polarization preferences observed in data. We address this by placing \(J/\psi\) and \(\phi\) in one soft-wall model on the planar limit of a five-dimensional equal-spin Myers--Perry (MP) AdS black hole, computing spectral functions and spin alignment within the same current-correlator framework; the nonrotating results of Sheng et al. [Phys. Rev. D 110, 056047 (2024)] are recovered at \(a=0\). At \(T=0.15~\mathrm{GeV}\), \(J/\psi\) retains a clear resonance peak, whereas \(\phi\) shows no narrow peak and instead behaves as a broad distribution consistent with unstable \(s\bar{s}\) pairs. For \(J/\psi\) along \(z\), rotation enhances the positive deviation of \(\rho_{00}^{h}\) from \(1/3\) at low and intermediate momenta but suppresses it at high momenta; along \(x\), the effect is small. For \(\phi\), rotation enhances the negative deviation, more along \(z\) than along \(x\). The opposite helicity-frame signs and the opposing azimuthal and rapidity trends of the global alignment provide a reference for interpreting data: trends inconsistent with these would challenge the simplest single homogeneous rotating-medium interpretation. We distinguish model-dependent numerical details from qualitative features stable within this model class.
papers.reason: Examines holographic spin alignment of vector mesons in rotating black hole backgrounds, adjacent to QCD medium and hadron polarization studies.

papers.title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
papers.abstract: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partial\phi)^4/\Lambda^4$ and $g_6(\partial\phi)^6/\Lambda^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.
papers.reason: Derives dispersion relations and eikonal scaling for a scalar EFT, touching on formal positivity bounds and dispersion relations.

papers.title: Unitary $KK$ and $K\pi$ inputs for an amplitude analysis of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay
papers.abstract: Charge-Parity Violation (CPV) is expected in three-body charm decays. In particular, in the singly Cabibbo suppressed decay process $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$; in which an amplitude analysis is required to understand the dynamics of Final State Interactions (FSI) and the mechanism that can generate CPV. In this work, we show the prospects of analysing recent data from the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN, with a precise theoretical model expected to reveal CPV mechanisms. Previous analyses of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay were unable to satisfactorily describe the data using the Isobar Model. Currently, LHCb has a sample of charmed meson decays with around 100 million events for the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay, so a more robust phenomenological model is needed to describe such a large data set. The present model has allowed the inclusion of hadronic FSI and will, in prospect, introduce three-body effects, overcoming some limitations of the Isobar Model, and has all factors necessary to reveal the presence of CPV. To do so, it factorizes the weak vertex separated in leading topologies and relies on extensions of Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory to describe FSI. As a proof-of-concept, a toy dataset of the S-wave of the most recent amplitude analysis of $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$, by the CLEO-c collaboration, was fitted with this model. From fits to model-independent parametrizations of scattering amplitudes, the parameters of the FSI amplitudes were fixed, and the production parameters of the weak vertex were then obtained from the fit to the toy dataset, yielding a good agreement between the data and our model.
papers.reason: Discusses hadronic final-state interactions and resonant chiral perturbation theory in charm decays, which is adjacent to understanding non-perturbative hadronic dynamics.

papers.title: Renormalization and Factorization Scale-Invariant Predictions for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process at $B$ factories
papers.abstract: We perform a NNLO perturbative QCD analysis for exclusive double charmonium production $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ within the NRQCD factorization formalism using the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC). It is well known that this charmonium process suffers poor pQCD convergence, as well as large renormalization scale uncertainty. The PMC is used to remove conventional renormalization scale uncertainty. Based on two fundamental physical processes of charmonium, $J/\psi\rightarrow e^+e^-$ and $\eta_c\rightarrow\gamma\gamma$, and using the NNLO perturbative results together with experimental measurements, we extract the factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix elements for $J/\psi$ and $\eta_c$. Combining these two matrix elements with the factorization-scale-dependent short-distance coefficient, we obtain predictions that are independent of the factorization scale for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. Our predictions agree with the measurement from the BaBar collaborations within errors. Remarkably, we provide a new way to eliminate conventional renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. We further demonstrate that the slow convergence of the pQCD series is an intrinsic property of this double-charmonium process.
papers.reason: Applies the Principle of Maximum Conformality to NNLO pQCD analysis of exclusive double charmonium production, relevant to QCD resummation techniques.

papers.title: Pionization experiments in light nuclei
papers.abstract: The zero-energy antiproton absorption in light nuclei is considered. The ratios $R_{n/p}$ of antiproton-neutron versus antiproton-proton capture rates in the lightest nuclei $^2$H, $^3$He and $^4$He are analyzed, both from the experimental results and from some selected theoretical models. These models are used as key input in determining the level shifts and widths of the lowest states. We establish the capture orbit in $^3$He to be states of angular momentum $L=2$. Several N-\={N} optical potentials are used to compute the $R_{n/p}$ values for several heavy nuclei and the results are found to be consistent with the data. However, the old chamber experiments studying pionization in Helium, are not consistent with models. Only the Paris potential is likely to succeed provided baryonia states predicted by this model are better understood.
papers.reason: Examines zero-energy antiproton absorption and capture rates in light nuclei, relevant to low-energy nuclear physics and potentials.

papers.title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
papers.abstract: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.
papers.reason: Studies cold quark matter and hybrid stars with a symmetry-preserving contact interaction, relevant to dense matter EOS for neutron stars.

papers.title: Birefringence in non-linear electrodynamics emerging from a Lorentz-symmetry violation scenario
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classical properties of a non-linear electrodynamics that emerges from one loop effective action for fermions coupled to an antisymmetric background tensor, that breaks the Lorentz symmetry in the model. The conservation laws are obtained through the Belinfante-Rosenfeld energy-momentum tensor in the non-linear electrodynamics that provides the energy density, the Poynting vector, the linear momentum and the stress tensor. In particular, this Lorentz symmetry violation breaks the symmetric index of the energy-momentum tensor, but it preserves the gauge invariance, as we expect. We introduce the prescription of a magnetic background field, that we consider constant and uniform. For propagation effects, the model is linearized by the magnetic background. This prescription allows us investigations of the plane wave propagation in the presence of an external magnetic field. In this context, we obtain the constitutive relations of the material medium, that behaves like an bi-anisotropic medium. Thereby, we calculate the refractive index whose one of the solutions show the total absorption of the wave in the medium. Using the wave equation for linear polarization, we investigate the birefringence phenomenon when the linear wave polarization changes with the magnetic background direction. The birefringence is so related to one of the spatial component of the LSV tensor in which we estimate through the PVLS experiment. We use one of the dispersion relations to obtain the kinematic of the Compton effect in the presence of the LSV parameter.
papers.reason: Investigates classical properties and birefringence in non-linear electrodynamics emerging from Lorentz-symmetry violation, connecting to precision low-energy tests.

papers.title: Quasi-normal Modes and Instabilities of Rotating Relativistic Stars
papers.abstract: We derive the basic equations suitable for the coupled fluid--spacetime eigenvalue problem from the second-order action in full general relativity and accurately determine quasi-normal modes of a variety of rapidly rotating stars with outgoing-wave boundary conditions. For MIT-bag strange stars, the spectrum realizes Chandrasekhar's instability picture, with distinct Chandrasekhar--Friedman--Schutz and Jacobi-like neutral conditions and the transition to dynamical bar-mode growth. For neutron stars, we determine the $f$-, $r$-, and other inertial-mode spectra and their radiative damping or growth times. Interactions between $f$- and inertial modes reveal avoided crossings and exchanges for radiative damping or growth rates. We locate quasiradial collapse thresholds through a static stability analysis and independently verify them by tracking the fundamental $F$-mode frequency to zero, clarifying that the central density at the onset of the dynamical instability is always larger than that of the secular instability for uniform rotation. Our formalism and numerical implementation can also resolve highly damped $w$-modes.
papers.reason: Determines quasi-normal modes and instabilities of rapidly rotating neutron stars and strange stars, relevant to dense matter and gravitational waves.

papers.title: Carbon-Reaction Constraints on Stellar Evolution: White-Dwarf Heating, Carbon-Burning Products, and Black-Hole Masses
papers.abstract: The effects of ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}+{}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ fusion and ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma){}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ capture on stellar heating, composition, and black-hole masses are examined. Rates from a published Bayesian analysis of carbon fusion are used in calculations with MESA. In an accreting carbon--oxygen white dwarf, the Bayesian rates move the point at which nuclear heating equals combined neutrino and surface photon losses to slightly larger stellar masses and higher central temperatures and densities. At an accretion rate of $10^{-7}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median gives a central temperature approximately $2.57\%$ higher and a central density $18.9\%$ higher than the calculation using the standard CF88 rate. A separate calculation follows carbon burning in an initially $20\,M_\odot$, $Z=0.0142$ star. Relative to the CF88 rate with MESA's standard division between proton and alpha channels, the Bayesian-median rate with the proton-to-alpha ratio of Yang et al. increases the neon-20 mass remaining at central carbon depletion by $10.8\%$ and decreases the sodium-23 mass by $28.7\%$.
